This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Gobo City|ja|御坊市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|ja|熊野古道|12=draft}}, particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=draft}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|12=draft}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|12=draft}}, is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=draft}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|12=draft}}, and five others | rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Gobo City|ja|御坊市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|ja|熊野古道|12=draft}}, particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=draft}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|12=draft}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft}}, is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=draft}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|12=draft}}, and five others | rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Gobo City|ja|御坊市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|ja|熊野古道|12=draft}}, particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=draft}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|12=draft}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft}}, is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=draft}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|12=draft}}, and five others | rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Gobo City|ja|御坊市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodō|ja|熊野古道|12=draft}}, particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|12=draft}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|12=draft}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the {{ill|Jōkyū War|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the {{ill|Kishū Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|12=draft}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|12=draft}}, is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|12=draft}}, {{ill|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|12=draft}}, and five others | rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}

revision.text:
本項目では、[[和歌山県]][[御坊市]]に所在する'''九十九王子'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == {{Main|九十九王子}}
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路|紀伊路・中辺路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が御坊市にある王子を扱う。
== 御坊市の九十九王子 == 御坊市の九十九王子は6社。[[上野王子 (御坊市)|上野王子]]は別項参照。
=== 善童子王子 === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|善童子王子]] '''善童子王子'''（ぜんどうじおうじ）は、[[九十九王子 (日高町)#高家王子|高家王子]]から、西川にかかる王子橋をわたって県道を南西に進んだところに小祠が祀られている。
『[[中右記]]』[[天仁]]2年（[[1109年]]）10月19日条に「連同持王子」にて大般若経があったと記し、「熊野道之間愚記」（『[[明月記]]』所収）[[建仁]]元年（[[1201年]]）10月10日条に「田藤次」、『民経記』[[承元]]4年（[[1210年]]）4月26日条に「伝童子」、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]5年（[[1473年]]）の『九十九王子記』に「善童子王子」とあるほか、[[仁和寺]]蔵の『熊野縁起』（[[正中 (日本)|正中]]3年〈[[1326年]]〉）は准五体王子であるとしている<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">平凡社[1997: 490]</ref>。
近世の記録では[[寛政]]年間の寺社調に御神体が木像であったとある<ref>西[1987: 123]</ref>ほか、『[[紀伊続風土記]]』には、方1[[間]]の本殿、長床、薬師堂があり、村人から出王子または出童子と呼ばれ、[[湯河氏|湯河家]]から社領・神主領の寄進を受けていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_490"/>とある。富安荘4ヶ村の氏神として崇敬されていたことから富安王子とも呼ばれたが、[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に湯川神社に合祀された<ref name="Heibon_1997_490"/><ref>長谷川[1997: 91]は合祀を[[1907年]]（明治40年）としている。</ref>。市指定史跡（[[1970年]]〈[[昭和]]45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/17.html | title=善童子王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 御坊市富安1347
=== 愛徳山王子 === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|愛徳山王子跡]] '''愛徳山王子'''（あいとくさんおうじ）は善童子王子から[[道成寺]]方面に進んだ、八幡山の北側にある。現地はミカン畑の中で、愛徳山王子跡地石碑と愛徳山王子碑が並んで立つ。1908年（明治41年）、近隣の吉田八幡神社に合祀された<ref>長谷川[1997: 91]</ref>。市指定史跡（1970年〈昭和45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/18.html | title=愛徳山王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 御坊市吉田2167
=== 九海士王子 === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|九海士王子]] '''九海士王子'''（くあまおうじ）は八幡山の南麓にある。本来の旧社地はミカン畑になったため、旧社地の東側に遥拝所を設け、小祠と海女王子（あまおうじ）社地の石碑が祀られている<ref name="Nishi_1987_125">西[1987: 125]</ref><ref name="Hasegawa_1997_92">長谷川[1997: 92]</ref>。
「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月10日条に「クワマ王子」、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条に「久和万」、文明5年（1473年）の『九十九王子記』に「桑間崎」とあるほか、仁和寺蔵の『熊野縁起』（正中3年〈1326年〉）はクアマの名を記している<ref>平凡社[1997: 231]</ref>ほか、『和歌山県聖蹟』にはクリマの名が挙げられている<ref name="Nishi_1987_125"/>。近世後期の史料には、九海士王子を道成寺伝説の一部に取り入れ、道成寺の観音像を海中より引き上げた海女に因むとしているが、九海士王子ないし海士王子の名で呼ばれるようになるのは近世のことである<ref name="Heibon_1997_232">平凡社[1997: 232]</ref>。1908年（明治41年）、吉田八幡神社に合祀された<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_92"/>。
旧蔵の神像は道成寺にて宮子姫像として祀られているが、[[アマテラス|天照大神]]像であったと推定されている<ref name="Heibon_1997_232"/>。市指定史跡（1970年〈昭和45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/19.html | title=海士王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 御坊市吉田2263-1
=== 岩内王子 === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|岩内王子跡]] '''岩内王子'''（いわうちおうじ）は九海女王子から[[紀勢本線]]の線路と[[日高川]]を越えた、日高川左岸にある。
『中右記』天仁2年（1109年）10月19日条に石内荘司宅に宿をとったとあるが参詣の記録はなく、「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月10日条に「渡河いわうち王子」、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条に石内王子参詣と記される他、近世には也久志波（やくしば）王子（『紀伊続風土記』）・焼芝（やけしば）王子（『九十九王子記』、[[享保]]15年〈[[1730年]]〉）と呼ばれていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_101">平凡社[1997: 101]</ref>。
『中右記』には石内から塩屋までの道が日高川の増水で通行不能になったとあり<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/>、他にも『紀伊続風土記』に「此地河流変遷し岩内王子の社地滅没して後世小社を此に建しといふ」<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/><ref>西[1987: 126]</ref>と述べられているように、旧社地はしばしば日高川の氾濫による水害を受けていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/>。1908年（明治41年）、熊野神社（御坊市熊野）に合祀され、青年会館の前に焼芝王子神社旧跡碑が遺されている<ref>長谷川[1997: 94]</ref>。
* 御坊市岩内字田畑515
=== 塩屋王子 === {{神社 | 名称 =塩屋王子神社 | 画像 =[[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | 所在地 =和歌山県御坊市北塩屋1145 | 位置 = | 祭神 =[[アマテラス|大日孁貴神]]・[[イザナミ|伊弉冉命]]ほか5柱 | 社格 =村社 | 創建 =不詳 | 別名 =美人王子 | 例祭 =10月19日（渡御・獅子舞・馬駆け） }} '''塩屋王子'''（しおやおうじ）は、岩内王子から南西に進んで、日高川支流の王子川右岸丘陵上にある。
[[藤原為房]]の熊野参詣記には塩屋にて宿をとったと記されているが参詣の記はなく、史料上の初見は『中右記』天仁2年（1109年）10月20日条に「至塩屋王子社奉幣」とあるものである。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月11日条に参詣の記事がある他、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条、仁和寺蔵の『熊野縁起』（正中3年〈1326年〉）にその名がある<ref name="Heibon_1997_427">平凡社[1997: 427]</ref>。近世には美人王子と呼ばれ（『九十九王子記』、享保15年〈1730年〉）、境内には『紀伊続風土記』を編纂した紀州藩藩儒[[仁井田好古]]撰の王子祠記碑が建てられた<ref name="Heibon_1997_427"/><ref>西[1987: 127]に碑文掲載あり。</ref>。
地元では今日でも美人王子の名で呼ばれ、美人王子の名の由来として、祭神の大日孁貴神（[[アマテラス|天照大神]]）の神像が美人であるからという説<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_95">長谷川[1997: 95]</ref>、[[白河天皇|白河院]]が熊野参詣の途上で歌会を催した（『[[新古今集]]』）<ref name="Heibon_1997_427"/>ことに見られるような景勝地であるからという説（『和歌山県聖蹟』）<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_95"/>などがある。
塩屋王子神社の境内は、和歌山県指定史跡（1958年〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書| publisher=和歌山県教育委員会 |url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkinen.html |title=県指定文化財・記念物 |accessdate=2009-09-27}}</ref>されたが、2018年（平成30年）2月13日に、史跡登録名称「[[熊野参詣道]][[紀伊路]]」の構成資産の一部として、「塩屋王子跡」が国の[[史跡]]に指定された<ref name=oji>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/kanko/bunkarekisi/bunka/ahibunka/shiseki/1382690305117.html|title=熊野参詣道紀伊路（塩屋王子跡、愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道）|accessdate=2020.1.3|publisher=御坊市 教育委員会 生涯学習課}}</ref>。社叢（神社林）は、暖地性の常緑樹林で沿海暖地の天然林があり、市指定天然記念物（1979年〈昭和54年〉5月28日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書|publisher=御坊市教育委員会 生涯学習課|url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/kanko/bunkarekisi/bunka/ahibunka/tennenkinen/1382692234318.html|title=塩屋王子神社の社叢|accessdate=2020.1.3}}</ref>。
=== 上野王子 === {{See|上野王子 (御坊市)}}
== 周辺情報 == === 愛徳山王子跡参詣道 === 愛徳山王子跡周辺には熊野古道としての土面路区間が残されており、史跡「[[熊野参詣道]][[紀伊路]]」の構成資産の一部として指定されている<ref name=oji />。 <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道 File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|愛徳山王子跡隣接竹林道 </gallery>
== 注 == {{Reflist|2}}

== 御坊市の九十九王子 == 御坊市の九十九王子は6社。[[上野王子 (御坊市)|上野王子]]は別項参照。
=== 善童子王子 === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|善童子王子]] '''善童子王子'''（ぜんどうじおうじ）は、[[九十九王子 (日高町)#高家王子|高家王子]]から、西川にかかる王子橋をわたって県道を南西に進んだところに小祠が祀られている。
『[[中右記]]』[[天仁]]2年（[[1109年]]）10月19日条に「連同持王子」にて大般若経があったと記し、「熊野道之間愚記」（『[[明月記]]』所収）[[建仁]]元年（[[1201年]]）10月10日条に「田藤次」、『民経記』[[承元]]4年（[[1210年]]）4月26日条に「伝童子」、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]5年（[[1473年]]）の『九十九王子記』に「善童子王子」とあるほか、[[仁和寺]]蔵の『熊野縁起』（[[正中 (日本)|正中]]3年〈[[1326年]]〉）は准五体王子であるとしている<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">平凡社[1997: 490]</ref>。
近世の記録では[[寛政]]年間の寺社調に御神体が木像であったとある<ref>西[1987: 123]</ref>ほか、『[[紀伊続風土記]]』には、方1[[間]]の本殿、長床、薬師堂があり、村人から出王子または出童子と呼ばれ、[[湯河氏|湯河家]]から社領・神主領の寄進を受けていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_490"/>とある。富安荘4ヶ村の氏神として崇敬されていたことから富安王子とも呼ばれたが、[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に湯川神社に合祀された<ref name="Heibon_1997_490"/><ref>長谷川[1997: 91]は合祀を[[1907年]]（明治40年）としている。</ref>。市指定史跡（[[1970年]]〈[[昭和]]45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/17.html | title=善童子王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 御坊市富安1347
=== 愛徳山王子 === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|愛徳山王子跡]] '''愛徳山王子'''（あいとくさんおうじ）は善童子王子から[[道成寺]]方面に進んだ、八幡山の北側にある。現地はミカン畑の中で、愛徳山王子跡地石碑と愛徳山王子碑が並んで立つ。1908年（明治41年）、近隣の吉田八幡神社に合祀された<ref>長谷川[1997: 91]</ref>。市指定史跡（1970年〈昭和45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/18.html | title=愛徳山王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 御坊市吉田2167
=== 九海士王子 === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|九海士王子]] '''九海士王子'''（くあまおうじ）は八幡山の南麓にある。本来の旧社地はミカン畑になったため、旧社地の東側に遥拝所を設け、小祠と海女王子（あまおうじ）社地の石碑が祀られている<ref name="Nishi_1987_125">西[1987: 125]</ref><ref name="Hasegawa_1997_92">長谷川[1997: 92]</ref>。
「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月10日条に「クワマ王子」、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条に「久和万」、文明5年（1473年）の『九十九王子記』に「桑間崎」とあるほか、仁和寺蔵の『熊野縁起』（正中3年〈1326年〉）はクアマの名を記している<ref>平凡社[1997: 231]</ref>ほか、『和歌山県聖蹟』にはクリマの名が挙げられている<ref name="Nishi_1987_125"/>。近世後期の史料には、九海士王子を道成寺伝説の一部に取り入れ、道成寺の観音像を海中より引き上げた海女に因むとしているが、九海士王子ないし海士王子の名で呼ばれるようになるのは近世のことである<ref name="Heibon_1997_232">平凡社[1997: 232]</ref>。1908年（明治41年）、吉田八幡神社に合祀された<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_92"/>。
旧蔵の神像は道成寺にて宮子姫像として祀られているが、[[アマテラス|天照大神]]像であったと推定されている<ref name="Heibon_1997_232"/>。市指定史跡（1970年〈昭和45年〉5月12日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書 | publisher=御坊市教育委員会 | url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/gobo/1120ka/bunkazai/19.html | title=海士王子跡 | accessdate=2009-09-27 }}</ref>。
* 御坊市吉田2263-1
=== 岩内王子 === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|岩内王子跡]] '''岩内王子'''（いわうちおうじ）は九海女王子から[[紀勢本線]]の線路と[[日高川]]を越えた、日高川左岸にある。
『中右記』天仁2年（1109年）10月19日条に石内荘司宅に宿をとったとあるが参詣の記録はなく、「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月10日条に「渡河いわうち王子」、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条に石内王子参詣と記される他、近世には也久志波（やくしば）王子（『紀伊続風土記』）・焼芝（やけしば）王子（『九十九王子記』、[[享保]]15年〈[[1730年]]〉）と呼ばれていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_101">平凡社[1997: 101]</ref>。
『中右記』には石内から塩屋までの道が日高川の増水で通行不能になったとあり<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/>、他にも『紀伊続風土記』に「此地河流変遷し岩内王子の社地滅没して後世小社を此に建しといふ」<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/><ref>西[1987: 126]</ref>と述べられているように、旧社地はしばしば日高川の氾濫による水害を受けていた<ref name="Heibon_1997_101"/>。1908年（明治41年）、熊野神社（御坊市熊野）に合祀され、青年会館の前に焼芝王子神社旧跡碑が遺されている<ref>長谷川[1997: 94]</ref>。
* 御坊市岩内字田畑515
=== 塩屋王子 === {{神社 | 名称 =塩屋王子神社 | 画像 =[[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | 所在地 =和歌山県御坊市北塩屋1145 | 位置 = | 祭神 =[[アマテラス|大日孁貴神]]・[[イザナミ|伊弉冉命]]ほか5柱 | 社格 =村社 | 創建 =不詳 | 別名 =美人王子 | 例祭 =10月19日（渡御・獅子舞・馬駆け） }} '''塩屋王子'''（しおやおうじ）は、岩内王子から南西に進んで、日高川支流の王子川右岸丘陵上にある。
[[藤原為房]]の熊野参詣記には塩屋にて宿をとったと記されているが参詣の記はなく、史料上の初見は『中右記』天仁2年（1109年）10月20日条に「至塩屋王子社奉幣」とあるものである。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月11日条に参詣の記事がある他、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月26日条、仁和寺蔵の『熊野縁起』（正中3年〈1326年〉）にその名がある<ref name="Heibon_1997_427">平凡社[1997: 427]</ref>。近世には美人王子と呼ばれ（『九十九王子記』、享保15年〈1730年〉）、境内には『紀伊続風土記』を編纂した紀州藩藩儒[[仁井田好古]]撰の王子祠記碑が建てられた<ref name="Heibon_1997_427"/><ref>西[1987: 127]に碑文掲載あり。</ref>。
地元では今日でも美人王子の名で呼ばれ、美人王子の名の由来として、祭神の大日孁貴神（[[アマテラス|天照大神]]）の神像が美人であるからという説<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_95">長谷川[1997: 95]</ref>、[[白河天皇|白河院]]が熊野参詣の途上で歌会を催した（『[[新古今集]]』）<ref name="Heibon_1997_427"/>ことに見られるような景勝地であるからという説（『和歌山県聖蹟』）<ref name="Hasegawa_1997_95"/>などがある。
塩屋王子神社の境内は、和歌山県指定史跡（1958年〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書| publisher=和歌山県教育委員会 |url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkinen.html |title=県指定文化財・記念物 |accessdate=2009-09-27}}</ref>されたが、2018年（平成30年）2月13日に、史跡登録名称「[[熊野参詣道]][[紀伊路]]」の構成資産の一部として、「塩屋王子跡」が国の[[史跡]]に指定された<ref name=oji>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/kanko/bunkarekisi/bunka/ahibunka/shiseki/1382690305117.html|title=熊野参詣道紀伊路（塩屋王子跡、愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道）|accessdate=2020.1.3|publisher=御坊市 教育委員会 生涯学習課}}</ref>。社叢（神社林）は、暖地性の常緑樹林で沿海暖地の天然林があり、市指定天然記念物（1979年〈昭和54年〉5月28日指定）<ref>{{Cite web|和書|publisher=御坊市教育委員会 生涯学習課|url=http://www.city.gobo.wakayama.jp/kanko/bunkarekisi/bunka/ahibunka/tennenkinen/1382692234318.html|title=塩屋王子神社の社叢|accessdate=2020.1.3}}</ref>。
=== 上野王子 === {{See|上野王子 (御坊市)}}
== 周辺情報 == === 愛徳山王子跡参詣道 === 愛徳山王子跡周辺には熊野古道としての土面路区間が残されており、史跡「[[熊野参詣道]][[紀伊路]]」の構成資産の一部として指定されている<ref name=oji />。 <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道 File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|愛徳山王子跡隣接竹林道 </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
{{Kujūku Ōji}}

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
{{Kujūku Ōji}}

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
{{Kujūku Ōji}}

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
{{Kujūku Ōji}}

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
{{Kujūku Ōji}}

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]

<!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all t]] == About Kujūku Ōji == {{Main|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}
'''Kujūku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of shrines located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly along the {{ill|Kiiji|ja|紀伊路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}} and {{ill|Nakahechi|ja|中辺路|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakahechi|qq=}} routes, rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by Kumano Shugendō practitioners, who guided imperial and noble pilgrims traveling to Kumano. They served as places for prayers and protection.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jōkyū War]] of 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} declined significantly, and with the deterioration of the Kiiji route, many shrines fell into ruin. During the Muromachi period, Kumano pilgrimages lost their prominence, and despite attempts at restoration by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishū Domain]] during the Edo period, decline continued. Further loss of sites occurred due to the State Shinto system after the Meiji era, mergers of shrines, and urbanization.
This article specifically discusses the shrines among Kujūku Ōji located in Gobō City.
== Kujūku Ōji in Gobō City == Gobō City has six Kujūku Ōji shrines. For {{ill|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|ja|上野王子 (御坊市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)|qq=}}, see separate entry.
=== Zendōji Ōji === [[File:善童子王子.jpg|thumb|Zendōji Ōji]] '''Zendōji Ōji''' (善童子王子) is located southwest of Ōji Bridge over the Nishigawa River, with a small shrine.
Historical records include references in "Chūyūki" (1109), "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kujūku Ōjiki" (1473), and listed as a semi-fifth-level Ōji in "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref name="Heibon_1997_490">Heibonsha [1997: 490]</ref>. It was locally revered, merged into Yukawa Shrine in 1909, and designated as a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Tomiyasu 1347
=== Aitokusan Ōji === [[File:愛徳山王子跡.jpg|thumb|Aitokusan Ōji]] '''Aitokusan Ōji''' (愛徳山王子) is north of Hachiman-yama hill near Dōjōji Temple. The site, now a citrus orchard, has stone monuments. It merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908 and became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2167
=== Kuama Ōji === [[File:九海士王子.jpg|thumb|Kuama Ōji]] '''Kuama Ōji''' (九海士王子) is on the southern foothills of Hachiman-yama. Originally within a citrus orchard, a worship place was established nearby. Historical mentions include "Kumano Michi no Aida Guki" (1201), "Minkeiki" (1210), and "Kumano Engi" (1326)<ref>Heibonsha [1997: 231]</ref>. It was merged into Yoshida Hachiman Shrine in 1908. The original statue, thought to represent [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], is now enshrined in Dōjōji as Princess Miyako. It became a city historic site in 1970.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Yoshida 2263-1
=== Iwauchi Ōji === [[File:岩内王子跡.jpeg|thumb|Iwauchi Ōji]] '''Iwauchi Ōji''' (岩内王子) is located on the left bank of the Hidaka River. Historical records date back to 1109, mentioning frequent damage from flooding. It was merged into Kumano Shrine (Gobō City) in 1908. A historical marker remains.
* Address: Gobō-shi, Iwauchi-aza Tabata 515
=== Shioya Ōji === {{infobox religious building | name = Shioya Ōji Shrine | image = [[File:塩屋王子 02.jpeg|200px]] | address = Gobō-shi, Kitashioya 1145 | deity = {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|アマテラス|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}}, [[:en:Izanami|Izanami]], and five others | Rank = Village Shrine | founded = Unknown | alternate names = Bijin Ōji | festival = October 19 (Procession, Lion Dance, Horse Racing) }} '''Shioya Ōji''' (塩屋王子) is on a hillside by the Ōji River, historically noted from 1109. Locally known as Bijin Ōji, theories suggest its name comes from the beautiful deity statue or scenic beauty. It is a Wakayama Prefectural Historic Site (1958) and part of the National Historic Site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji" (2018). Its shrine forest is a city-designated natural monument (1979).
=== Ueno Ōji === {{See|Ueno Ōji (Gobō City)}}
== Nearby Information == === Aitokusan Ōji Pilgrimage Path === Original sections of Kumano Kodō remain around Aitokusan Ōji and are part of the national historic site "Kumano Sankeimichi Kiiji"<ref name=oji />. <gallery> File:愛徳山王子跡北東参詣道.jpg|Aitokusan Ōji Northeast Path File:愛徳山王子竹林道.jpg|Bamboo Grove near Aitokusan Ōji </gallery>

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Gobō, Wakayama|Gobo City]] [[:en:Kumano Nachi Taisha|Kujūku Ōji]]
